A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 30-page versions of the same RL-SPH paper. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I.

before.justification: v7 reports original ILP benchmark experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, generalization tests, and solver-integration results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v8 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark tables and supplementary experiments in Appendices H and I.7.

M1.justification: The two-phase reward system, ILP-GT architecture, feasibility-aware search, action space, and training procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same IS, CA, SC, MVC, and NBI benchmarks, cross-problem scenarios, MIPLIB instances, and distribution, size, and density shifts.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: DHF, FP, RHF, and RENS in Table 1; PAS, DDIM, DiffILO, and the retained classical baselines in Table 2. Appendix solver comparisons also retain the same methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.3 removes the ×100 factor from the stated primal-gap formula, changing its defined scale from percentage to ratio. Splits, budgets, and testing procedures remain unchanged. This is a reported metric correction; the PDFs do not establish recomputation of experiments.

E4.justification: The reward-directionality analysis, search and architecture ablations, robustness tests, presolving analysis, hyperparameter studies, and qualitative cases are retained unchanged, including Appendix I.7's movement-magnitude experiment.

E5.justification: Existing ± reporting and SCIP randomization settings are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes repeated-run information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Reported numerical entries, rankings, curves, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Tables retain their PG (%) labels and values despite the formula correction; no new performance gain or loss is reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of primal gap in Section 4.1.3 is revised by removing ×100. Proposition 1, its assumptions and Appendix A proof, and the remaining mathematical derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction adds 'a conditional feasibility guarantee' as a gloss on reward-feasibility alignment. Proposition 1 and Appendix A already state that conditional result in v7, so the contribution's substantive scope is unchanged. The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability limitations remain unchanged, including cross-problem failures, scaling bottlenecks, and untested nonlinear constraints. The added conditional-guarantee wording restates conditions already documented for Proposition 1.

D1.justification: Pseudocode, implementation hyperparameters, hardware and software specifications, training times, data-generation instructions, and code-access information remain unchanged in the corresponding appendices.

R1.justification: v8 adds Berthold's 2013 'Measuring the impact of primal heuristics' to the bibliography and cites it for primal gap and primal integral in Section 4.1.3. The other cited works and research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The contribution summary gains a short explanatory phrase, and the metrics paragraph receives localized editing associated with the formula and citation changes. The section organization and appendix narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added reference reflows the bibliography across pages 10–13, with small paragraph-position changes elsewhere. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: Removing ×100 from the PG definition resolves the percentage-versus-ratio mismatch with PI's retained convention of PG = 1 when no feasible solution exists; tables still explicitly display PG as percentages. The added metric citation and explanation of the existing conditional result modestly improve attribution and clarity. These are limited improvements to otherwise unchanged scientific content.
